To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Ocean Colour Climate change Initiative (OC CCl) has produced an ocean colour data set that has been validated against in situ data and that the uncertainties have been quantified on a pixel by a pixel basis, and that the data set can now be used in climate research, including the development of models and algorithms that are needed to improve the products.

the approach adopted to generate the ocean colour products for the OC CCI project is robust, that the products meet the requirements of climate users, and that the uncertainties are quantified and are available to users.

a) an ocean colour time-series that meets the climate requirements can be generated by processing ocean colour data using the algorithms that are best-suited for climate studies, and b) a consistent time series can be generated by band shifting the remote sensing reflectances of different sensors to a common waveband, and c) the uncertainties of the products can be quantified and mapped at the same spatial resolution as the data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the generation of ocean colour data that meet the climate user requirements, including the generation of uncertainties.
the production and validation of a long term time series of ocean colour data that is suitable for use in climate studies.
generating ocean colour data that are suitable for climate research and that meet the user requirements, including those of marine ecosystem modellers.
